title: Stream delivery recovery: chunk replay, backpressure diagnostics, and guardrails
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Summary: On 2026-03-09 a spike in sustained request concurrency against a small set of tenants exposed a regression in our streaming layer that resulted in: (a) abrupt client disconnects with partial token emission, (b) incorrect KV cache eviction under high sequence churn, and (c) incomplete backpressure propagation from the proxy to the runtime. This ticket tracks follow-up engineering work: root cause verification, short-term mitigations, implementation of durable chunk-level replay and acknowledgements, and improved observability and runbooks.

Impact: Multiple customer integrations observed truncated responses or silent disconnects during high-throughput bursts. Initial telemetry shows a peak disconnect rate of 0.9% across affected endpoints, with per-tenant error spikes up to 6%.
timeline:
2026-03-09 02:17 UTC - Alert: Elevated stream termination rate from SRE alerting.
2026-03-09 02:22 UTC - Pager rotation; triage identifies streaming disconnect spike correlated with a model-serving autoscaling event.
2026-03-09 02:45 UTC - Engineering mitigations: increased proxy read timeout, temporarily disabled aggressive KV-cache trimming, and routed heavy tenants to a higher-capacity pool.
2026-03-09 05:10 UTC - Full incident declared resolved for customer-facing errors; follow-up tasks opened for durable fixes.
2026-03-10 - Initial RCA and action list drafted.
2026-03-12 - Design review with runtime and proxy teams; consensus on chunk ACK + idempotent chunk markers.
2026-03-14 - Implementation PR for added metrics and a small proxy config change opened for review (see links).
root_cause: We identified a regression introduced in runtime scheduling (PR merged 2026-02-28) that changed the sequence of KV cache touch and eviction under transient high-concurrency sequences. This produced two compounding issues: 1) under certain eviction timing, a request's tail context was lost and the runtime emitted partial token sequences while cleaning up internal state; 2) the reverse-proxy flow-control code path did not surface per-chunk backpressure signals reliably when kernel-level write buffers filled, so clients saw socket-level closes rather than graceful stalls. The combination of partial token emission and abrupt closes manifested as \"partial-token disconnects\" in customer logs.
resolution_summary: Short-term: emergency proxy timeout increase and routing heavy tenants to dedicated pools reduced customer-visible disconnects to <0.12% within 3 hours. KV-cache trimming was disabled for affected pools and a hotfix that re-ordered cache touch semantics was rolled to a canary group.\nMedium/Long-term: we will implement chunk-level acknowledgement + replay with idempotency tokens, strengthen backpressure propagation and observable signals from the proxy to runtime, add targeted chaos tests, and update runbooks and SLA dashboards.
action_items:
1) Add stream-level metrics and event tags: 'stream.chunk.sent', 'stream.chunk.acked', 'stream.chunk.retransmit', 'stream.conn.drop.reason' and wire into our streaming dashboard. Owner: Liam Chen. Due: 2026-03-21.
2) Implement per-chunk ACK and replay in runtime plus idempotency markers to avoid double-emission on replay. Design doc approved; implement PR. Owner: Aisha Rao. Estimate: 8. Due: 2026-04-02.
3) Restore and harden KV-cache semantics: ensure cache touch happens before eviction decisions for active sequences; add regression test covering eviction under sequence churn. Owner: Priya Nair. Due: 2026-03-25.
4) Proxy backpressure improvements: add socket-level write buffer monitoring and translate to explicit gRPC/HTTP flow-control signals to runtime. Owner: Oscar Mendes. Due: 2026-03-28.
5) Run targeted chaos experiments that simulate sustained concurrency and partial network drops; add to pre-release test suite. Owner: EngOps (Darwin Soto). Due: 2026-03-30.
6) Update streaming runbook: include triage playbook for partial-token reports, steps to re-route tenants, and escalation paths. Owner: SRE lead (Maya Patel). Due: 2026-03-18.
7) Customer communication: draft post-incident summary and mitigation notes for affected customers; coordinate with CS. Owner: Kate Alvarez (Customer Success). Due: 2026-03-16.

acceptance_criteria:
- End-to-end tests show replay succeeds and produces exactly-once visible token sequences in 100% of test runs.
- Production disconnect rate for streaming endpoints reduced to <=0.1% sustained and per-tenant spikes limited to <=1% during stress.
- New metrics present on dashboard and linked to alerts: missing ack rate, retransmit rate, avg chunk RTT, conn drop reasons.
- Runbook published and on-call trained; customer comms sent to impacted customers with follow-up plan.
notes:
Review feedback from design review: prefer client-side idempotency marker semantics to avoid complex server-side dedupe for multi-model fanout (noted by Deputy Eng Lead). Trade-off: client markers require SDK updates; agreed to implement server tolerance for older clients for 3 weeks.
Progress updates: small hotfix for cache touch ordering shipped to canary 2026-03-11; initial metrics PR opened 2026-03-13; chunk-ACK design accepted 2026-03-12.
Risks: Chunk-level replay increases potential duplicate token emission if clients do not reconcile; mitigation will be idempotency marker + SDK patch and documented fallback.
Reviewers: Aisha Rao (runtime), Priya Nair (cache), Oscar Mendes (proxy), Maya Patel (SRE).
